themes.claim: A fixed meeting time narrowed the search for three organizers
themes.counter_evidence: P2, P4 and P6 named the branch first and could shift the time. All six discussed their starting constraint.

evidence.quote: Tuesday at four was the only time all four of us could do. I checked two branches for that hour.
I picked East Branch first because everyone can get there after class. We moved the meeting to Thursday when the room was free.
We already had an hour between classes. I asked which branch could fit us in then.
I only looked at Central. It's on the one bus route we can all use, so I asked for the next open afternoon there.
We agreed on Saturday morning first. I would have booked at either of the two branches near us.
West was the only branch I considered. I could move the afternoon if that was the only place my group could walk to.

themes.claim: A specific room need prompted checks before booking
themes.counter_evidence: P3 took a staff suggestion without asking about seats or equipment. P5 relied on prior experience with the room. All six discussed room selection.

evidence.quote: The room title didn't say how many seats it had. I called the desk before filling in the form.
I asked the desk whether there was a whiteboard before I agreed to the slot. We needed to work through equations together.
I took the room the librarian offered. I didn't ask about seats or equipment.
I asked if there was a way to reach the room without stairs before I booked it. I would have tried another room if the answer was no.
We'd used that room before. I looked for the opening and booked it without checking the room details again.
I couldn't tell whether five of us would fit. I stopped at the form and called the branch to ask.

themes.claim: Booking details gave organizers something to pass along
themes.counter_evidence: P4 told people in person because they were there. P5 sent only a brief update because the group knew the room. All six discussed sharing. P6 still received an entrance question after sharing the time and room.

evidence.quote: I forwarded the confirmation because it had the branch and room number together. Nobody had to ask which building.
I wrote down the room number from the call. I sent it with the time in our group chat.
I used the booking slip to tell the group which floor to meet on.
We were already together when I booked, so I just told everyone the room right there.
Our group already knew the room, so I just said we were on for Saturday in the chat.
After the call I had the time and room in a text from the desk. I copied both into the group chat.
